meaning_en: to shape, to form (dough, clay) into its final shape; fig.: to work out in detail
definition_de: einer Masse (Teig, Ton) die endgültige Form geben (den Teig zu Brötchen ausformen); übertragen: etwas im Detail ausarbeiten (eine Idee ausformen). Seltener als 'formen'; typisch in Back- und Handwerkssprache.
example_de: In der Backstube formt der Bäckerlehrling den Teig zu gleichmäßigen runden Brötchen aus.
example_en: In the bakehouse, the baker's apprentice shapes the dough into even, round rolls.
visual_idea: Collocation 'den Teig (zu Brötchen) ausformen', the standard phrase in baking: a shapeless lump of dough at one side and a tray of identical round dough balls at the other, so lump to final shape (aus- = fully worked out) is visible in one frame, and the result does not depend on drawing hands precisely. Rejected: shaping clay on a potter's wheel (reads as 'töpfern') and 'eine Idee ausformen' (abstract).
image_prompt: in a German bakery workshop a young baker in white clothes and a white cap stands at a floured wooden table; on the left a big shapeless lump of pale dough, in the middle a large black baking tray with twenty identical smooth round dough balls in neat rows, he rolls the last small ball between his floury palms above the tray; flour dust in warm light, early morning
negative_prompt: text, letters, watermark, signature, caption, blurry, extra fingers, deformed hands, cluttered background, multiple panels
video_prompt: in a bakery workshop a young baker tears a piece from a big lump of dough, rolls it between his palms into a smooth round ball and places it in the last free spot on a tray full of identical dough balls; static camera
